rationale: prctl(PR_SET_NAME/PR_GET_NAME) thread-name semantics: one localized error-vs-truncate divergence, in a syscall area no earlier round has taken (prctl is untouched; prctl01/02/07 are already enabled, so the syscall is wired and only this edge case diverges). Host baseline 8/8 pass, and the host run shows exactly the behaviour under test: an 18-byte name 'prctl05_test_xxxxx' is silently truncated to 'prctl05_test_xx' (15 bytes). In Asterinas, kernel/src/syscall/prctl.rs:65-71 handles PR_SET_NAME with read_cstring(read_addr, MAX_THREAD_NAME_LEN=16), and read_cstring (kernel/src/context.rs:202-224) fails with ENAMETOOLONG when no NUL byte appears within max_len. Linux's PR_SET_NAME instead uses strncpy_from_user(comm, arg2, TASK_COMM_LEN-1), which returns negative only on a fault and truncates silently otherwise. So tcase 2 makes prctl return -1 and the test TFAILs at prctl05.c:45 while tcase 1 ('prctl05_test', 12 bytes) passes -- a 4-pass/1-fail shape rather than a broad subsystem gap. The pieces a fix needs already exist: ThreadName::set_name_as_bytes (kernel/src/process/posix_thread/name.rs:29-33) already truncates to MAX_THREAD_NAME_LEN-1, and a non-erroring truncating reader (read_cstring_until_end, kernel/src/util/read_cstring.rs:57) is already in the tree. The procfs half of the test is already satisfied: 'comm' is in TidDirOps::STATIC_ENTRIES (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/procfs/pid/task/mod.rs:106), and PidDirOps inherits it via lookup_static_child, so both /proc/self/comm and /proc/self/task/<tid>/comm resolve. Preferred over the alternatives for exactly this narrowness: prctl10 needs PR_SET_TSC/PR_GET_TSC (absent, plus SIGSEGV-on-rdtsc -- a feature, not a bug); fcntl27 needs F_SETLEASE, which has no FcntlCmd variant at all; utime06/utimes01 both set .needs_rofs; epoll_ctl04/05 need epoll nesting-depth and cycle detection (a whole ep_loop_check equivalent, and adjacent to the already-taken epoll_ctl02); mincore*, mlock01, munlock01, splice01/02, tee01 and remap_file_pages01 are unwired in kernel/src/syscall/arch/x86.rs, so all are missing-feature verdicts.
